task: Make a value that must be handed over (pending puts, a claim to answer) impossible to drop on some path
do: Mark the type `#[blaze::linear]` and each function that ends it `#[blaze::consumes]` (crates/hir-ty-linear, docs/v2/plan/design/linear.md); the borrow check then refuses every non-unwinding path that drops one and names its consumers. Give it a `Drop` only when that `Drop` is a right abandonment for an error exit (a claim given back); a runtime bomb in `Drop` makes `?` drop the value silently. Never build it out of a closure given to an unmarked generic (`with_store(.., || Claim {..})`, `Option::map`): return the parts and build it after.
why: There is no `blaze::owed` lint: linear types already are the language primitive for this, enforced as semantics with no `#[expect]`. A second mechanism would be two homes for one concept.
